speaker: john_heminges
text: The almanac is open. New moon, which it knew before we did. Lent begins on the fifth of March. That is five playing weeks, if we mean to have them.

speaker: john_heminges
text: I have the afternoons counted. Twenty-eight before Lent, and I want four of them for the comedy.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Then give me the time to learn him. I want three full weeks for Berowne, for he never stops talking.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Hilary ends on the twelfth of February. After that the Hall is shut, and a share of the town rides home.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: They do not all ride. We may trust the Inns on a day that is not a term day.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Thursday the twentieth of February. Give me that, and I will have him from the first oath to the last song.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Thursday the twentieth, then. A term-less day, and we trust the Inns to come anyway.

speaker: will_kemp
text: And what jig follows it, when your Frenchmen have done being sorry?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: A comedy needs none.

speaker: will_kemp
text: None. That is a small cloud, and I am the man standing under it. The yard stays for the bells after the gentlefolk bow.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: The songs are the end of it. I have the pointing in my hand since this morning. I will not set a hornpipe on the owl's last note.

speaker: thomas_pope
text: The Rose will play till they're stopped.

speaker: john_heminges
text: The Rose has no mayor sleeping next door to its poet.

speaker: george_bryan
text: Shrove Tuesday is the fourth of March. We stop that night. We do not play into Lent and tempt the Mayor.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Sir John sits three rows ahead of me on a Sunday. I am not handing him a playing Thursday after the ash.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Four is the want. The twentieth is the day I will write first. Shrove Tuesday is the day I will write last. Between them the book can grow without my reading a catalogue at this candle.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Four days, no jig, and a Thursday with no term to lean on. You have made a lean feast, John. I have eaten leaner.

speaker: thomas_pope
text: The two boys stand at three shillings the week, and not a penny of it is on tonight's leaf. Their mothers know the difference between a promise and a coin.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Three full weeks from Tuesday's reading is more than the twentieth gives me. I am taking the twentieth. I am not pretending the lines are short.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: They are not short. That is why the three weeks were asked, and why the twentieth is as far as the fast allows.

speaker: george_bryan
text: Ash Wednesday the fifth. After that, nothing of ours inside the walls. I would rather a clean stop than a clever one.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Then it is set. I have no share to read you from today's boxes, and I am not opening a coffer because an almanac agreed with us.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: The boys will have both notes in the throat by the twentieth. I am not promising it for tomorrow. Tomorrow is only Friday, and Friday already has the paper.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: French Doctor was the Rose today. We did not go. Tomorrow's Shrew is not mine.

speaker: will_kemp
text: A day you are not in is a day I have survived before. You will survive Friday. Try not to write a tragedy about it.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Thou hast talked less than Berowne, Will, which is the kindest thing I can say after two.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am done. The day I owe at home is still not known, and this table does not know it for me.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Enough. The twentieth. Shrove Tuesday. Four afternoons wanted, and none of them paid for tonight. God give us the Inns, and a Mayor who sleeps through February.
